name: bark
summary: The outside of a living tree: furrowed, fibrous, damp at the bottom and never smooth anywhere.
why: Metallic 0.0, roughness 0.88 - just above rock's 0.86 and the roughest thing in the
library apart from foliage. Bark is the least reflective surface in Lorencia: it is dry
dead fibre with air in it, and even wet it does not shine, it darkens.
Grain is brushed and runs along v, which is up the trunk. This is the one material where
the direction is not a judgement call - MU's tree sheet is vertical furrows from top to
bottom, and a cast grain across it would cancel the only structure the art has.
Depth 0.35, the deepest declared here, above rock's 0.30. On the world profile the depth
scales a normal read off the art's own luminance rather than a generated pattern, and
bark is the best case that reading has: those furrows are drawn as near-black lines and
